messages:
maria: FYI ALB in us-west-2 started deregistering ~18 edge targets ~2m ago, app traffic errors spiked. Not seeing CPU/GPU pressure — looks network/discovery related :thinking_face:
ash: I see the same alerts. ALB TargetHealth shows 'Unhealthy' with reason 'Invalid response' for a bunch of pod IPs. Any recent DNS or kube-proxy changes?
maria: We had a CoreDNS rollout 3m before this (scaled to 1->3) to address some query latency. timeline aligns.
liam: Adding logs — aws-load-balancer-controller events show it re-registered targets after EndpointSlice updates. I think the controller picked new IPs that weren't actually serving (readiness probes not ready yet).
juniper: Oof — headless svc for edge-proxy returns endpoints that briefly map to node IPs during kube-proxy churn. Past cause was kube-proxy warmup where iptables rules aren't populated; controller sees EndpointSlice and registers the IP immediately.
maria: Pulled EndpointSlices at time of incident, here's snippet:
```
NAME                          ENDPOINTS   AGE
edge-proxy-abc-xxxxx          3           5m
edge-proxy-abc-xxxxx-ep1     1 (nodeIP)   30s
edge-proxy-abc-xxxxx-ep2     2 (podIP)    90s
```
ash: so ALB was probing the nodeIP that responded with the host's default vhost -> 404/502, hence Unhealthy. ALB then removed target.
liam: Repro steps I used: scale coredns down/up quickly in staging, then watch endpoints flip order and alb-targets change.
juniper: Quick mitigation: roll CoreDNS back to previous stable replicaset and pause the LB-controller reconcile to let endpoints settle. Did that and saw targets re-register healthy after ~40s.
maria: Confirmed rollback fixed immediate 502s. But we need a permanent fix: controller should gate registration on endpointReady or we should avoid headless service exposing hostIPs to controller during transient state.
ash: Filed infra/issue #4321: "aws-lb-controller registers EndpointSlice IPs before readiness confirmed" with logs/trace. Suggest options: (1) add readiness gating in controller, (2) change headless svc to ClusterIP + DNS for pod access, (3) increase CoreDNS rollout cadence/slow down autoscaler.
liam: Also opened runbook pr: runbook/edge-lb-dns-flap.md with checklist (check CoreDNS rollout, kubectl get endpoints, kubectl get endpointslices, pause controller, rollback coredns).
maria: Note for postmortem: include why kube-proxy warmup + headless service + aggressive coredns scaling combined to create a window where endpoints advertise nodeIPs.
juniper: Longer-term: patch controller to ignore endpoints with hostNetwork/nodeIP when target-type=ip for this service, or add a 10-15s stabilization window after EndpointSlice change before reconciling target group.
devops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0882 (priority P2) — assigned to eng-infra.
maria: Thanks all. Action items: 1) keep CoreDNS at stable for now (ash), 2) add controller gating proposal (liam), 3) ops runbook improvements (juniper). I'll follow up with a short postmortem in #postmortems later today. :white_check_mark:
